title: nntp: XGET command — fetch arbitrary IPFS block by CID
description:
Why: XCID resolves a message-id to a CID but does not fetch content by CID. Clients that obtain a CID (from XCID, from X-Usenet-IPFS-CID headers, or from any external source) have no way to retrieve the corresponding IPFS block through the NNTP interface. This command makes the NNTP reader a gateway to the full IPFS network.

What:
Add XGET <cid> command to the NNTP reader.
- Syntax: XGET <cid-string>
- Response on success: 290 <cid-string> followed by a synthetic RFC 5322 MIME message in the standard NNTP dot-stuffed multi-line format:
    From: ipfs-gateway@<configured hostname>
    Subject: IPFS:<cid>
    Message-ID: <<cid>@ipfs.local>
    X-Usenet-IPFS-CID: <cid>
    MIME-Version: 1.0
    Content-Type: application/octet-stream
    Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
    <blank line>
    <base64-encoded block bytes>
    .
- Response codes:
    290: article follows
    430: CID not found on local IPFS node
    501: syntax error (not a valid CID string)
- Advertise XGET in CAPABILITIES.
- Valid in any session state after authentication; no group or article pointer required.

MIME wrapping with base64 is required because NNTP dot-stuffed multi-line is not binary-safe. Wrapping also keeps the format consistent with the JMAP blob download and IMAP X-USENET-IPFS-GET responses.
